_readme: SPAM BLOCKLIST for the public forms (contact, become-a-retailer,
retailer check-in, health practitioners, Erospain booth, GDPR).
Edit this file, commit, and redeploy the server. No code change needed.
Matching is case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.
emails          exact addresses            'jane@store.com'
domains         everything @ that domain   'spam-farm.example'
names           exact full names           'Jane Doe'
messageContains substring in the message   'crypto investment'
mode:  'reject' returns 403 and tells the sender to email us directly, so
someone blocked by mistake still has a way through. 'silent'
returns a normal success and quietly drops the submission, which
is better against bots but leaves a wrongly-blocked human with no
signal at all. Start with 'reject'.
repeatLimit: the automatic stopper, applied to everyone whether or not
they are listed above. Counts DELIVERED submissions only.
maxSubmissions  refuse once this many have already gone through
windowDays      how far back to count; 0 means forever
scope           'form' counts per form, 'all' counts across every
form together
matchOn         'email-or-name' also catches someone who keeps
their name and rotates the address. Note this
conflates two different people with a common
name — a second 'John Smith' can be refused
because of the first. Set 'email' to match on
the address alone.
A malformed file is ignored with a loud server log and every form keeps
working — a typo here must never take the site's forms down.
